title: Separate small complete-segment entropy from stationary recurrence
statement: On N0 let pi_n=e^-1/n!,d0=0,d_n=(n+1)^-2 for n>=1,p_n=[(n+1)(n+2)^2]^-1,q_n=1-d_n-p_n. Detailed balance pi_n p_n=pi_(n+1)d_(n+1) gives the reference Poisson law with every fixed moment. For0<eta<=1/2,a=eta²/4,add delta_n=a/(n+2) to upward probabilities and subtract it from q_n for n>=1; row0 and down probabilities stay fixed. Since q_n>=2/3 these are valid kernels. Each rowTV<=a/3; forwardKL<=2a/3 via qlog(q/(q-delta))<=2delta and reverseKL<=4a=eta² via(p+delta)log(1+delta/p)<=delta+delta log(1+delta/p),log(1+delta/p)<=log2+2log(n+2). Give each marked event an independent unit exponential holding time,including self-events. ENTIRE first-event marked-path laws have the same entropy bounds; each segment costs exactly one firing and mean time1,total expected firings throughT equalT and N_t<=n0+Pois(T) pathwise. Yet any stationary probability for the perturbed birth/death chain must have zero boundary flux and rho_(n+1)/rho_n=pprime_n/d_(n+1)>=a(n+2); its tail weights eventually at least double,so no invariant probability exists. Thus two-sided small segment entropy,Poisson reference moments and polynomial segment/finite-horizon costs do not imply perturbed positive recurrence. CRUCIAL LIMIT: pprime_n/p_n is UNBOUNDED; these probabilities do NOT arise as the specified fixed small independent mass-action coefficient perturbations. This is an abstract inference counterexample,not a universal elementary-compiler negative or a correction to the valid conversion-segment entropy theorem.
